thread.title: Dow Jones Futures Rally Despite Apple Stock Dive On Apple Earnings; Starbucks Signals Breakout | Investor's Business Daily

author: ED CARSON
title: Dow Jones Futures Rally Despite Apple Stock Dive On Apple Earnings; Starbucks Signals Breakout | Investor's Business Daily

organizations.name: dow jones futures today dow jones

text:
Dow Jones futures and S&P 500 futures rose solidly Friday morning while Nasdaq futures also advanced, signaling the stock market rally will continue even with tech giant Apple ( AAPL ) retreating. President Donald Trump reportedly has asked his staff to draft a a China trade deal. Starbucks ( SBUX ), Fortinet ( FTNT ), Arista Networks ( ANET ), Shake Shack ( SHAK ) and Universal Display ( OLED ) were big movers on late Thursday earnings as well. Apple stock, Shake Shack, Fortinet and Universal Display all fell sharply, while Starbucks stock signaled a breakout.
X Three of these stocks have an IBD Composite Rating of at least 95. Apple stock and Fortinet stock boast a best-possible 99 Composite Rating. Starbucks stock has a 95 Composite Rating. Shake Shack had a 92 CR heading into earnings.
Dow Jones Futures Today Dow Jones futures jumped 1.2% vs. fair value, erasing late Thursday losses. S&P 500 futures rose 0.8%. Nasdaq 100 futures, down more than 1% at one point late Thursday, climbed 0.2%. Remember that overnight action in Dow futures and elsewhere doesn't necessarily translate into actual trading in the next regular session. That's been true during the stock market correction.
China Trade Deal Hopes Trump has asked his administration to draft a possible China trade deal, as he prepares for a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Group of 20 meeting in late November, Bloomberg News reported. Stocks rallied Thursday in part because Trump tweeted that he had a good phone call with Xi. That comes after reports that Trump was planning to escalate the China trade war if the Xi meeting did not go well.
Meanwhile, in addition to China trade deal talk, Apple earnings and other late-Thursday reports, Friday brings earnings from Alibaba ( BABA ) and Dow components Exxon Mobil ( XOM ) and Chevron ( CVX ). Alibaba earnings were mixed but shares rose early Friday. Also Friday: the October jobs report.
Stock Market Correction Isn't Over The stock market correction isn't over, but a new rally attempt continued Thursday. The major averages rose again, while more top stocks broke out past buy points. However, there has not yet been a follow-through day to confirm the new stock market rally. That could happen has soon as Friday. But until that follow-through day happens, investors should be cautious about any new purchases.
Apple Earnings Apple earnings rose 41% to $2.91 a share in its fiscal fourth quarter on sales of $62.9 billion, up 20%. That was the third straight quarter of accelerating earnings growth and the eighth quarter of faster sales gains.
Analysts expected Apple earnings per share of $2.78 a share, with revenue at $61.599 billion.
Apple sold 46.89 million iPhones, a little light. But the average price jumped 28% to $793, well above views.
Apple sees holiday-quarter revenue of $89 billion to $93 billion, below views of $93.02 billion.
Apple stock fell 6% early Friday.
Shares of the Dow Jones, S&P 500 and Nasdaq component closed up 1.5% to 222.22 on the stock market today . Apple stock settled just above its 50-day line. Shares have held up well in the stock market correction. The relative strength line , which tracks a stock's performance vs. the S&P 500 index, has been at or near record highs.
Starbucks Earnings Starbucks earnings rose 13% to 62 cents a share as revenue grew 11% to $6.3 billion. Same-store sales rose 3%, 4% in the Americas and a bullish 4% in the U.S.
Analysts expected Starbucks earnings of 59 cents per share on sales of $6.2 billion. Consensus Metrix expected 2.2% global comps growth, including 2.8% in the Americas.
For 2019, Starbucks expects EPS of $2.61-$2.66 on 5%-7% revenue growth. The midpoints beat analyst views for $2.62 per share and 5% sales growth.
Starbucks stock jumped 9.2% to 64 early Friday. That suggests Starbucks will clear a 59.90 buy point from a handle in a messy nine-month consolidation.
Fortinet Earnings Fortinet earnings leapt 75% to 49 cents a share as revenue grew 21% to $453.90 million. Wall Street forecast Fortinet earnings of 42 cents on revenue of $450.9 million.
The cybersecurity firm's Q4 guidance midpoint also is slightly above analyst targets.
But Fortinet stock fell 6.2% late after closing up 1.8%. The Fortinet stock chart looks a lot like Apple's. The stock also closed just below its 50-day line, but it's holding up well after peaking in early October.
Arista Earnings Arista earnings jumped 30% to $2.11 a share in Q3. Revenue rose 29% to $563.3 million. Analysts expected Arista earnings of $1.84 a share and sales of $548.3 million.
Arista Networks sees Q4 revenue of $588 million, just above estimates of $586 million.
Arista stock shot up 11% early Friday, signaling a move above its 50-day and 200-day lines. Shares closed up 4.6% to 240.96, their third advance after hitting a 2018 low Monday.
Universal Display Universal Display earnings rose 71% to 8 cents a share, with revenue up 26% to $77.55 million. But analysts expected Universal Display earnings of 64 cents on revenue of $91.4 million.
The OLED technology and components maker sees full-year revenue of $240 million to $250 million, far below views for $304.6 million.
Universal Display stock plunged 26% before the open. Shares rose 5.4% to 129.65 Thursday, nearing a 130.70 buy point. That followed a sharp sell-off from January's peak of 209.
Shake Shack Earnings Shake Shack earnings were flat at 17 cents a share, with sales rising 26.5% to $119.6 million, both topping views. But same-store sales fell 0.7%, defying forecasts for a 0.9% rise.
Shake Shack nudged up full-year sales and comps targets, but slightly below views.
Shake Shack stock fell 3.3% late. Shares rose 3.6% Thursday to 54.78.
